commit message:
Make Particle(arg) == Particle(Particle(arg))

This allows all of the arguments in a list to be converted to a
Particle more simply: `[Particle(particle) for particle in particles]`
instead of saying `if not isinstance(particle, Particle) else
particle`.

We had some discussion (see #486) about whether or not the same
instance should be returned, or if a copy should be returned.  The
decision was to create a copy so that it would behave like
numpy.array.  My hesitation is that list comprehensions like the one
above would create lots of Particle instances for the same particle,
when in actuality only one instance of Particle('electron') would be
necessary.  However, there is a chance that returning the same object
in memory would trip users up, so a more rigorous way of doing this is
to just create a copy.

Co-authored-by: Colby Haggerty <colbych@udel.edu>

Which is, of course, a smart decision from them. So I'm removing that one from test dependencies, but it'll still be specified in the tox env we have for codespell. So it should be fine.

commit message:
Reformat _Isotopes

Previously, the _Isotopes dictionary in isotopes.py was built using a
helper function that took in the symbol, name, atomic number, mass
number, stability, half-life, and isotopic abundance and then returned
a small dictionary for each isotope that was then put into the big
_Isotopes dictionary.  The motivation behind this strategy was to
reduce the size of the file.  However, a more significant disadvantage
was that it was not very readable since you had to go back and look at
the top of the file to see what each value represented.

I reformatted _Isotopes so that each attribute is on a different line.
I also renamed/shortened some of the keys since that could be done so
without reducing readability (e.g., 'atomic_mass' became 'mass' and
'isotopic_abundance' became 'abundance').  I had to update the keys
elsewhere in the atomic subpackage.

commit message:
Hack defaultdict equality testing in Particle

In Particle.__eq__, I compare the Particle._attributes defaultdicts.
However, two defaultdicts test to be unequal if they have different
previously undefined keys that have been accessed.  This hack accesses
all of the defined keys in either defaultdict from the other
defaultdict, which allows == to work as intended.

author: Nick Murphy <namurphy@cfa.harvard.edu>
commit message:
Use dict comprehensions for helper atomic dicts

Previously the dicts to get the atomic symbol from either the element
name or the atomic number were spelled out in full.  However, the same
information was contained in the _Elements dict, so the data was being
repeated.  I changed these to dictionary comprehensions.

This formulation has the advantage that if the atomic number of
hafnium ever changes, we will only need to update it in a single
place.

commit message:
Add PlasmaPy contributors to credits.rst

This is a first draft of the contributors to PlasmaPy for our version
0.1.0 release.  This involved some detective work!  I found the names
primarily by searching through our git log and then looking at
people's GitHub profiles.  I also added some people who contributed to
the vision statement while it was on Google Docs, and thus do not have
any credits for their commits.

There are some people who made commits but who do not show up on
GitHub.  I did a quick web search and a possible cause may be that
those contributors' PRs were rebased, which caused the person doing
the rebasing to get recorded as making those commits on GitHub.  I do
not know if this is the case here.  When updating this page, we should
make sure to check both the GitHub contributors page as well as the
git log.

Also: I have not yet verified these names, so there may be mistakes!

commit message:
Refactor nuclear_reaction_energy

Originally, the function nuclear_reaction_energy required a string
containing the nuclear reaction as the sole argument.  In issue #110,
@jessicalostinspace suggested that the inputs be lists of the
reactants and products in the reaction which will make it easier to
iterate over different reactions.  This pull request implements this
suggestion.  I did require that reactants and products be keyword-only
arguments because there is potential for the two lists to get mixed
up, and the sign of the reaction is important.

I decided to keep the old API which has the argument being a string
representing the function, but with some ambivalence.  The advantage
of this is that it is much more human readable if we are doing a small
number of reactions.  The disadvantage is that it makes the
implementation a bit more complex.  I broke the code into different
functions so that the flow of the main part of the function is
smoother.

Electrons and positrons are now allowed in the reactions since they
are important for beta decays.

commit message:
Update type return annotations for Quantities

Previously I had been mixing up return annotations in the atomic
subpackage for functions and methods that returned Quantities.  The
return annotations for some were `-> u.Quantity` whereas others were
like `-> u.kg`.  For functions decorated with @u.quantity_input, it is
appropriate to use the latter return annotation.  I tried decorating
these functions with @u.quantity_input, but this led to errors since
the arguments and keywords are not Quantities themselves.  Instead, I
changed everything in the atomic subpackage to the former possibility
so that the return annotations are `-> u.Quantity` and don't mention
units..

commit message:
Update IonizationStates and tests

 - I changed __setitem__ to raise a TypeError for when a `dict` is
   used as a key.  One possibility for here would be to allow for a
   subset of base particles to have their ionic_fractions reset.

 - I updated __eq__ to account for nans and infs, and to check several
   different attributes besides ionic fractions.  There is some code
   repetition between here and IonizationState so we might want to
   extract these code chunks and put them into a different function
   that accounts for nans, infs, and Quantity objects.

 - I removed a clause from antiquity from when the n attribute was n_H
   and enforced to be the number density of hydrogen instead of the
   number density scaling factor.

 - The ionic_fractions attribute will now only be able to be set using
   a dict that contains all of the base particles that were previously
   being accounted for.  Item assingment seems to be a cleaner way to
   assign new ionic fractions to subsets of the old particles.  I
   expanded the docstring too.

 - I fixed a probable bug in the ionic_fractions setter that used a
   variable left over from a loop to check that the particles have
   the correct properties.

 - I removed a check that particle instances are sorted by atomic
   number and mass number because there is a test that checks this.

 - I removed the base_particles setter because this is set by
   ionic_fractions.

 - The main gap right now in testing is that tests of exceptions are
   missing.  I have begun adding and parametrizing tests of
   exceptions.  I also updated tests for equality, abundances &
   log_abundances, and that str and repr don't raise exceptions.

 - I created a new class for testing attribute assignment and
   reassignment after an IonizationStates instance was created with
   only the elements specified.  This class includes some tests of
   exceptions, and checks that certain attributes default to the
   specified values (i.e., kappa defaults to np.inf and T_e defaults
   to np.nan * u.K).  Right now the main thing that remains is to
   clean up and fill in gaps of tests of IonizationStates.  **yawn**

author: Dominik Stanczak <stanczakdominik@gmail.com>
commit message:
Halve runtime of classical_transport tests with one simple trick!

So it turns out if you put in a setup_method() into a Test class that's
run by Pytest, that setup_method is executed for every single method call.
This includes all the calculations involved in classical_transport
initialization, and anything else we are doing in preparation for
these tests.

If you just setup_method into a setup_class @classmethod, it's
going to get called once per class - and that means all the variables
in it are only going to be calculated once, and they'll be shared
across every instance of the class.

It was thus the only sane choice to go all out with this.

Reference material: https://docs.pytest.org/en/latest/xunit_setup.html

commit message:
Metadata updates prior to version 0.2.0 (#629)

* Remove obsolete top-level INSTALL.md file

We originally kept our installation directions in this file, but have
since moved the information to our docs directory.  We kept this file
in case it was linked to from anywhere else on the World Wide Web, but
it has been a long enough time that we can safely remove it.

* Update setup.cfg

* Update citation information

A recommended practice for scientific reproducibility is to cite the
specific version of software used for a project, and an established
practice is to cite a paper or informational resource that describes
it.  This commit updates CITATION.rst and the near-identical
docs/about/citation.rst to include both of these references.  We
previously decided to keep both of these files despite the duplication
to make it extra apparent how to cite PlasmaPy.

I changed plasmapy.__citation__ to be a list of DOI links, including
the standard reference from 2018 and version 0.2.0.  The metadata for
our releases on Zenodo could potentially change (for example, adding
the name of a contributor that wasn't known before), so a DOI is the
most robust way to go about it.

I reserved the DOI for version 0.2.0 on Zenodo, so the links to that
will not work yet.

to pass through in the annotated argument to the decorated function.
This may be useful in functions such as known_isotopes, where an
argument of None would indicate that this function should return all
known isotopes of every element.  Technically this is a misquote,
although practicality beats purity.

commit message:
Expand IonizationStates class

I added the capability to iterate over charge states, in which case I
used a `collections.namedtuple` with different attributes for the
integer charge, ionic fraction, and ionic symbol since these are the
most relevant values.  It might end up being reasonable to include the
number density in here too, if available.

Prior to this, I had set separate `rtol` and `atol` keyword arguments
and attributes for use with numpy.isclose.  I changed this to a sole
`tol` attribute because (1) for checking the normalization, absolute
and relative tolerances reduce to the same thing because the relative
tolerance is relative to one, and (2) for tiny abundances, the
absolute tolerance will be more relevant than the relative tolerance.
In calls to numpy.isclose, I explicitly set `rtol` equal to zero so
that it's clear that we're dealing with absolute tolerances and not
relative tolerances.

I defaulted `tol` to 1e-15 since at 1e-16 I got errors with
np.isclose.

commit message:
Move pytest helpers to subdirectory of utils

Our pytest helpers functionality has been in a single file in
plasmapy.utils, which means that the functionality in there is jumbled
together with a bunch of other unrelated things.  Putting it in its
own subdirectory will help with the organization.  I also split the
existing functionality in pytest.

I updated the namespaces for run_test, etc. in a bunch of test files
throughout the package.  I also made a few non-consequential changes
in the test files that I noticed, mostly removing unused import
statements.

I am planning on doing more refactoring to the pytest helpers
functionality, which will enable me to do some more refactoring of
tests.  The API for utils.pytest_helpers should be considered unstable
at the moment.

commit message:
Several improvements to OTS fitting (#2636)

* Update thomson.py

* Several changes (see notes)

- Changed `ion_mass` to `ion_mu` in lite function to support fitting this parameter (it is hard to fit very small numbers like the ion mass in kg)
- Changed the way the notch keyword in the lite function is applied to fix a bug.
- Changed _model function to look for `ion_mu` and `ion_z` in params instead of settings.
- Changed Model creation function to create fixed parameters for any `ion_mu` or `ion_z` parameters not set explicitly.  Remove old `ions` validation that doesn't apply anymore.
- Refactored tests to get rid of support changes, get rid of some warnings.
- Added a new test for explicitly setting `ion_mu` and `ion_z` as varying parameters.
-

* Roll back change of keyword in lite function: just do the multiplication in _model instead

* Create 2636.feature.rst

* Remove message kwarg in pytest.raises and pytest.warns

In pytest.raises, the message argument has been used to provide a test
failure message, but it has gotten confused with the match argument
which is used to check the message from the exception to be tested so
it is being deprecated.  I changed the usage to:

    with pytest.fails(SomeException):
        should_raise_exception()
	pytest.fails("should_raise_exception() did not raise anything")

Also, we had pytest.warns(..., message="...") at one point, though it

commit message:
Update __eq__ magic method in Particle class

The easiest way to implement __eq__ for the Particle class would
be to simply check if the particle symbol is the same between the
the two instances of the class.  However, a more detailed check
is desirable because it allows for more reliable testing of this
class.  In particular, this dunder method is really helpful in
making sure that particle aliases produce equivalent results
[e.g., that Particle('p') == Particle('proton')].  This method
also checks that if an exception is raised for one instance of
the class, then it also checks that an exception is raised for
the other instance of the class (without actually checking that
the same exact exception is raised).

author: Nick Murphy <namurphy@cfa.harvard.edu>
commit message:
Use ion_mass in nuclear_binding_energy

Prior to this, nuclear_binding_energy used isotope_mass as the mass of
the nucleus.  However, isotope_mass includes the masses of the bound
electrons, which should not be included in the nuclear binding energy.
This function now uses ion_mass and assumes that the isotope is fully
ionized.

There is at least one error at perhaps the 1e-5 level.  For Fe-56, the
function gave 492259.578 keV whereas the corresponding result on
Wikipedia is 492253.892 keV for a difference of 5.686 keV.  Plasma
physicists rarely need this level of accuracy in practice, but we
might still be able to get more accurate values for nuclide masses and
binding energies for any applications that need it.

be for physical particles).

commit message:
Update user installation doc page

I have been wavering between whether or not the user installation
instructions should be on the same page as the contributor
installation instructions.  Including all of the installation
instructions in one place may make it seem overwhelming to new users,
so right now I am thinking that it would make the most sense to direct
docs/install.rst to new users and docs/development/install_dev.rst to
new contributors.

The things that still need to be added to this page are instructions
on creating a conda environment to install PlasmaPy in, and
instructions on how to build PlasmaPy.

I don't think I have yet included all of the prerequisites for
building PlasmaPy.

Much of the reorganization and layout is inspired by Astropy's
installation instructions.

commit message:
Bring check_relativistic back to _boilerPlate

As it turns out, when we added z_mean to the arguments to coulomb_log,
we changed their order. z_mean now came in place of the old V argument.
And that means all the time, we were going with the default nan
velocity. Thus, the one for _check_relativistic was being calculated
off of the temperature (low for these cases). Thus, the warning
was correctly not firing - the velocity was too low for it to launch!

commit message:
Update sphinx-build flags for on/off RTD

This change makes it so that different flags get used for sphinx-build
depending on whether the Nox session is run on RTD or off of it.

Usually it is easier to parse the standard output when the `--quiet`
flag is used, so it is the default. Since it can be helpful to see the
full output, the RTD build does not use the `--quiet` flag.

The `--fail-on-warning` flag is not used on RTD because it makes it
harder to see the documentation preview, which can be really helpful.

commit message:
Add DOI and citation for source code (#541)

I recently archived the version 0.1.0 and 0.1.1 releases (as downloaded
sa.tar.gz files from GitHub) on Zenodo, so our source code has DOIs!  I
added the DOIs to our citation files and README, and unrelatedly updated
LaTeX formatting in __citation__.

Zenodo versioning includes DOIs for specific versions (Version DOIs) as
well as DOIs that cover all versions of an upload (Concept DOIs).  The
link from our README refers to the Concept DOI, while papers that use a
specific version of PlasmaPy should cite the appropriate Version DOI.

commit message:
Use @nox_uv.session in docs_upstream

This session previously took the names optional dependencies from
pyproject.toml without the version specifiers and passed them into
session.install(). The motivation was to avoid resolution conflicts
if an upper dependency limit had been put on the target package.
I believe that this is no longer necessary when using @nox_uv.session.
At the same time, it is helpful information to know that there is a
resolution conflict that will need to be fixed, and failing when that
happens will inform us about that problem.

commit message:
Add looponfailroots=plasmapy to setup.cfg

This allows running tests with pytest-xdist's `pytest --looponfail`
setting. What that does is run tests in a loop whenever a file is
modified,, but if some fail, it limits the next loop to those particular
tests. It's awesome.  Anyway, looponfailroots limits the file modified
detection to the plasmapy dir, which is reasonable here. I had it
trigger on vim creating those tags files I mentioned earlier.

Test consistency between different requirements files

the requirements directory.  There is some duplication of information,
but this duplication is necessary since the package requirements for
documentation tests, code tests, and the package itself differ.  When
we require a new package or update a minimum version, problems can
arise should we change one file but forget to change the others.  I
added some tests to check for common mistakes and inconsistencies for
when we make these updates.  I still need to add a few more to check
different files.

commit message:
Significant modifications to parameters.py + tests

Updating parameters.py to use _check_quantity and _check_relativistic
from utils subpackage.  The first checks to make sure an object is a
quantity with the correct units and acceptable numerical values.  The
second checks velocities to make sure they're not relativistic.  This
change greatly reduces the repetition of the same checks being done in
different functions, but should probably be changed into decorators at
some point after the universe has expanded a little more.

I removed an error in the calculation of gyroradii and inertial
lengths which were of the form of a velocity divided by an angular
frequency.  I used the dimensionless_angles equivalency from
astropy.units, which treats radians as 1.  Hence, the results were a
factor of 2*pi off.  The new equivalency list is [(u.cy/u.s, u.Hz)]
which yields the intended behavior.  Radians are weird.

I updated a lot of docstrings.  These still need to be checked.
Additionally, it would be great to have an understandable discussion
of the physics in each of the routines.  I still need to add upper &
lower hybrid frequencies.  The tests for parameters.py still need to
be extended and updated.

commit message:
Test tuple annotations in @particle_input

This test checks that functions decorated by @particle_input with an
argument that is annotated with (Particle, Particle) will pass through
the expected Particle instances.  In essence, this test checks that
using this tuple annotation will allow @particle_input to behave in
pretty much the same was as having two separate arguments that are
each decorated with Particle.

When setting this test up, we have to be careful because running
Particle('p+') == 'p+' will return True because the __eq__ magic
method for the Particle class allows comparisons with string
representations of particles.

commit message:
Adopt morally ambiguous defaults for pydocstyle

I added a list of the common default settings to setup.cfg also for
easy reference.

The general consensus in the discussion on Matrix is that it is more
readable to start the "one-liner" of a docstring on the line after the
""" rather than on the same line as the """, so I set that as the
default.

I also set it so that the "one-liner" can exceed one line, since I've
found there are occasions where even a concise description of the
physics involved in a function or class needs to take up more space
than that.

Move pytest helpers to subdirectory of utils (#674)

Our pytest helpers functionality has been in a single file in
plasmapy.utils, which means that the functionality in there is jumbled
together with a bunch of other unrelated things.  Putting it in its
own subdirectory will help with the organization.  I also split the
existing functionality in pytest.

I updated the namespaces for run_test, etc. in a bunch of test files
throughout the package.  I also made a few non-consequential changes
in the test files that I noticed, mostly removing unused import
statements.

I am planning on doing more refactoring to the pytest helpers
functionality, which will enable me to do some more refactoring of
tests.  The API for utils.pytest_helpers should be considered unstable
at the moment.

commit message:
Update Particle.__repr__

Make it so that this magic method returns a string that if evaluated
would result in an equal class (where equal is defined through the

commit message:
Update citation information

A recommended practice for scientific reproducibility is to cite the
specific version of software used for a project, and an established
practice is to cite a paper or informational resource that describes
it.  This commit updates CITATION.rst and the near-identical
docs/about/citation.rst to include both of these references.  We
previously decided to keep both of these files despite the duplication
to make it extra apparent how to cite PlasmaPy.

I changed plasmapy.__citation__ to be a list of DOI links, including
the standard reference from 2018 and version 0.2.0.  The metadata for
our releases on Zenodo could potentially change (for example, adding
the name of a contributor that wasn't known before), so a DOI is the
most robust way to go about it.

I reserved the DOI for version 0.2.0 on Zenodo, so the links to that
will not work yet.

commit message:
Have IonizationState.__getitem__ return namedtuple

Before this, I had IonizationState[value] return just a float for the
ionization fraction.  Now it returns a namedtuple with the integer
charge, ionic fraction, and ionic symbol.  This change is because the
integer charge, ionic fraction, and ionic symbol are all likely to be
needed, and to be consistent with the behavior as an iterator.

It may be worth changing this namedtuple (presently named State) into
a class.  There's also a need to create an IonizationStates class that
includes more elements.

nuclear_reaction_energy.

in test_import_helpers.py.

exceptions, whether or not we raise them or are trying to catch them.

PlasmaPy.  Hopefully this doesn't break the universe or anything. :-)

Update user installation doc page

I have been wavering between whether or not the user installation
instructions should be on the same page as the contributor
installation instructions.  Including all of the installation
instructions in one place may make it seem overwhelming to new users,
so right now I am thinking that it would make the most sense to direct
docs/install.rst to new users and docs/development/install_dev.rst to
new contributors.

The things that still need to be added to this page are instructions
on creating a conda environment to install PlasmaPy in, and
instructions on how to build PlasmaPy.

I don't think I have yet included all of the prerequisites for
building PlasmaPy.

Much of the reorganization and layout is inspired by Astropy's
installation instructions.

commit message:
Near completion of code for Coulomb_logarithm

I think I got Coulomb_logarithm to work, but at the cost of no longer
believing anything related to plasma transport theory ever again.  My
goal was to make the code as physics-based and as close to a
derivation as possible, so that users will understand why they should
never believe in plasma transport ever again either.

The choice of inner de Broglie wavelength using the reduced mass seems
reasonable, because for an electron-ion pair then the reduced mass
reduces to approximately the electron mass which corresponds to the
electron de Broglie wavelength which will be longer than the ion de
Broglie wavelength.

I put a bunch of (sometimes contradictory) references in a comment on
pull request #60 in the PlasmaPy GitHub repository.

I still have to finish documentation and add tests.  It would be good
to compare to the values in Table 5.1 of Spitzer (1962).

commit message:
Add return annotations in test_particle_input

When a function decorated by particle_input has the keywords Z or
mass_numb, the decorator raises an exception when more than one
argument is annotated with Particle in order to avoid ambiguity about
which particle the Z or mass_numb refers to.  However, the failure of
these tests shows that the exception is also unintentionally raised
when the decorated function has a return annotation of Particle.

commit message:
Metadata updates prior to version 0.2.0 (#629)

* Remove obsolete top-level INSTALL.md file

We originally kept our installation directions in this file, but have
since moved the information to our docs directory.  We kept this file
in case it was linked to from anywhere else on the World Wide Web, but
it has been a long enough time that we can safely remove it.

* Update setup.cfg

* Update citation information

A recommended practice for scientific reproducibility is to cite the
specific version of software used for a project, and an established
practice is to cite a paper or informational resource that describes
it.  This commit updates CITATION.rst and the near-identical
docs/about/citation.rst to include both of these references.  We
previously decided to keep both of these files despite the duplication
to make it extra apparent how to cite PlasmaPy.

I changed plasmapy.__citation__ to be a list of DOI links, including
the standard reference from 2018 and version 0.2.0.  The metadata for
our releases on Zenodo could potentially change (for example, adding
the name of a contributor that wasn't known before), so a DOI is the
most robust way to go about it.

I reserved the DOI for version 0.2.0 on Zenodo, so the links to that
will not work yet.

commit message:
Separate formatting functions out of pytest_helpers

Up until now, the functions that were used to do formatting were
enclosed in plasmapy.utils.pytest_helpers.  These functions included
call_string, which gives a string that can be used to call a function
(which is particularly useful for reproducing errors).  These
functions can be used more broadly than that, so I created a spinoff
module in plasmapy.utils.formatting.

Part of my motivation is to help us remove pytest as a hard
dependency.  I am hoping to have plasmapy.utils not depend on pytest
at all, while everything that depends on pytest can be held within
plasmapy.tests (which I am thinking can be a lot like astropy.tests).

commit message:
Allow IonizationState to accept an ion as an argument

Up until now, the IonizationState class has required the base particle
to be either an element or isotope.  However, there may be some cases
where we want to set the ionic fraction to be 100% of a particular
ion.  This pull request allows us to do things like
IonizationState("alpha"), in which case the base particle will be He-4
and the ionic fractions will be [0.0, 0.0, 1.0] (i.e., all He-4 atoms
are doubly charged).

Credit for the idea goes to:
Co-authored-by: Maurice Wilson <maurice.wilson@cfa.harvard.edu>

has been added. It receives a BaseType vector as adjacency matrix instead
of the 1/0 integer vector of InitializeVectorAsMaxCutCostFunction().

which assumes an integer max_value and transform all cut values to integers
in {0, 1, 2, ..., max_cut}.

commit message:
Feature/qubit ordering (#24)

Add the possibility of reordering the qubits at the level of the data storage.

Consider that we have N qubits distributed among 2^P processes.
Previously:
* the first M=N-P qubits were local
* the last P qubits were global
Now we can choose the qubit order for storage and therefore select any M qubits to be local.
This possibility helps reducing the simulation time by avoiding MPI communication overhead.

Implementation:
* Add distributed implementation of (symmetric) SWAP-like gates.
* Extend class Permutation.
* Add documentation inside qureg.hpp about storage conventions.
* 'qubit' indicates program qubits, 'position' indicates data qubits
* GetGlobalAmplitude(index) returns the amplitude corresponding to the global index in input, considering that such index is expressed in terms of program qubits while the actual state is stored according to the data qubit order.
* Add QubitRegister functions to permute qubits. For example PermuteQubits(), PermuteLocalQubits(), ...
* Add unit tests covering the class Permutation class and novel QubitRegister methods.

commit message:
Add extra feature related to qaoa for weighted maxcut (#9)

Specifically, the function InitializeVectorAsWeightedMaxCutCostFunction()
has been added. It receives a BaseType vector as adjacency matrix instead
of the 1/0 integer vector of InitializeVectorAsMaxCutCostFunction().
Furthermore, it returns the max weight of cut edges.
The weighted case does not work well with GetHistogramFromCostFunction()
which assumes an integer max_value and transform all cut values to integers
in {0, 1, 2, ..., max_cut}.

author: Pascal Jungblut <pascal.jungblut@ifi.lmu.de>
commit message:
Switch to C++ complex MPI types

`MPI_COMPLEX` and `MPI_DOUBLE_COMPLEX` are Fortran MPI datatypes (3.2.2,
table 3.1). `MPI_CXX_FLOAT_COMPLEX` and `MPI_CXX_DOUBLE_COMPLEX` directly
correspond to the C++ types `std::complex<float>` and
`std::complex<double>`, respectively (table 3.4).

This should improve the portability, e.g. Open MPI's BCast breaks at
runtime with `MPI_COMPLEX` in C++.
